subject: general
question: A train of length 299 m takes 12 seconds to pass another train 101 m long coming from the opposite direction. If the speed of the first train is 71 km/hr, then find the speed of the second train.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cover = Sum of lengths of both trains = 299 + 101 = 400 m

Relative speed in m/s = Total distance ÷ Time = 400 ÷ 12 = 100/3 m/s

Relative speed in km/hr = (100/3) × (18/5) = 120 km/hr

In opposite direction, Relative Speed = Speed₁ + Speed₂

Speed₂ = 120 − 71 = 49 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 49 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of Train 1 (L₁) = 299 m

Length of Train 2 (L₂) = 101 m

Time taken (T) = 12 seconds

Speed of Train 1 (S₁) = 71 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

Speed = Distance / Time

To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

 Train 1: 299 m 
 
 71 km/hr Train 2: 101 m 
 
 x km/hr 
• Total Distance = 299 + 101 = 400 m Time = 12 seconds 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 299 + 101 = 400 m

⇒ Relative Speed = Total Distance / Time

⇒ Relative Speed = 400 / 12 m/s

⇒ Relative Speed in km/hr = (400 / 12) × (18 / 5)

⇒ Relative Speed = (100 / 3) × (18 / 5)

⇒ Relative Speed = 20 × 6 = 120 km/hr

⇒ Since they are moving in opposite directions: S₁ + S₂ = 120

⇒ 71 + S₂ = 120

⇒ S₂ = 120 − 71

⇒ S₂ = 49 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 49 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ + V₂.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = |V₁ − V₂|.

Speed Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses another train or a bridge, the total distance covered is the sum of the lengths of both entities.
